issues_confirmed: nn/data_builder.py:451-466 — LEAKAGE_MAP has 6 keys but nn/evaluate.py:348-362 publishes 11 KEY_TARGETS; 7 published targets get no leakage handling at all. The 2026-09-28 item 1 fix IS present (sentiment cols in has_ticket, size_issue/damaged_in_transit cross-dropped for has_refund) and was verified by reading the map.

nn/data_builder.py:451 — no LEAKAGE_MAP['resolved_by'] key, so resolution_time_minutes survives as a feature. Counted from data/support_tickets.csv: bot-resolved resolution_time_minutes in [5,29] (n=504, mean 16.9), human-resolved in [60,1439] (n=700, mean 756.5), zero overlap; a single threshold at 29 gives 100% accuracy. msg_count (values 0/3/5) and customer_msg_count (0/2/3) are independent perfect 3-way separators. This is the whole of the Accuracy 1.0000 at REPORT.md:274.

REPORT.md:290 — states 'the channel a customer contacts through almost perfectly determines who handles them'. False: cross-tabbed support_channel vs resolved_by is chat 251h/168b, email 356h/259b, instagram_dm 93h/77b; majority-vote accuracy 0.5814, identical to the naive baseline 700/1204. support_channel tops the permutation ranking only because it is 'none' on 97.56% of rows, i.e. it is a has_ticket detector.

nn/data_builder.py:469-480 — resolved_by is the only ticket-derived column missing from FILTER_MAP, so it is scored against a 97.56% 'none' baseline (REPORT.md:277). customer_msg_count is also missing while msg_count is present.

nn/data_builder.py:451 — no LEAKAGE_MAP['resolution_time_minutes'] key, so resolved_by survives. Predicting the group mean of resolved_by (bot 16.9, human 756.5) gives RMSE 304.1 vs naive-mean RMSE 475.0; REPORT.md:310 publishes a model RMSE of 315, i.e. worse than the one-column lookup it calls '33% better than naive'.

nn/data_builder.py:451 — no LEAKAGE_MAP['product_type'] key. data/variants.csv weight_grams has exactly 6 distinct values across all 645 variants, each mapping to exactly one of the 6 product types (120g Cap, 280g Tee, 520g Sweatpants, 650g Hoodie, 850g Trainer, 900g Outerwear). Fully explains Accuracy 1.0000 at REPORT.md:245; REPORT.md:264 credits supplier_country and gross_margin_est instead, which are co-leaks (all top features are product/variant-level attributes broadcast onto line items).

nn/data_builder.py:204 — postcode_district is kept as a feature while city is a KEY_TARGET (nn/evaluate.py:361). All 40 postcode districts in data/addresses.csv map to exactly one city; majority-vote accuracy 1.0000 against a 75.0% London baseline. default_country is a partial leak at 80.6%. No number is published yet (REPORT.md:480 shows '—').
REPORT.md:480 — describes city as '20+ UK cities'. There are 11 cities and only London is in the UK (Madrid, New York, Chicago, Brooklyn, Los Angeles, Amsterdam, Dublin, Paris, Berlin, Rome).

nn/data_builder.py:68-69 — _load_refunds computes refund_variant_ids then discards it on the next line; the merge at :356 is on order_id, so refunds are labelled at order grain on a line-item table. Recounted: 5,843 refunds, no order refunded twice, every refund_line_items array has length exactly 1, and those orders contain 10,025 line items -> 4,182 rows (41.7% of the positive class) are mislabelled. REPORT.md:174's 'Positive rate (actual) 14.33%' is 10,025/69,956; the true rate is 8.36%.

data/refunds.csv — the fix for the above is viable: every refund's variant is present in its order's line items (0 misses in 5,843). 5,836 match exactly one line-item row and 7 match two, so the correct positive count is 5,850, not the 5,843 the 2026-09-28 TODO proposed asserting.

nn/model.py:174 vs :212-226 — all_preds/all_targets are reassigned at the top of every epoch's validation block, so after model.load_state_dict(best_weights) they still hold the FINAL epoch's predictions. The metric at :215-226 describes a discarded model, while permutation_importance (nn/estimator.py:514) and --save_model (:527) use the restored one. nn/evaluate.py:376-391 feeds the same stale arrays into every metric suite, so all of REPORT.md section 3 measures weights the run threw away.
nn/model.py:202-212 — if val_loss is NaN on epoch 1, 'inf - nan > min_delta' is False, so best_weights stays None and model.load_state_dict(None) raises a bare AttributeError.

nn/data_builder.py:536 — get_X_y types a single-valued column as binary because set(unique).issubset({0,1,True,False}) is satisfied by a one-element set. data/line_items.csv confirms quantity == 1 on all 69,956 rows, so --target quantity trains to completion then dies at nn/model.py:219 with 'Only one class present in y_true'. quantity is advertised as a headline target at nn/estimator.py:122.

nn/data_builder.py:240-244 — n_escalations counts a 'bot' message immediately followed by a 'human' one, but the senders in data/support_messages.json are customer (3,108), bot (1,204) and agent (700). There is no 'human' sender (same stale name at :231 and :252), so the count is identically 0 on all 1,204 tickets and therefore on all 69,956 rows. Renaming to 'agent' does not help: the transcripts have only two shapes, customer|bot|customer|agent|customer (700) and customer|bot|customer (504), so bot is never adjacent to agent. n_escalations is a FILTER_MAP target (:475), so --target n_escalations crashes exactly like quantity.

nn/evaluate.py:78 vs :321 — in make_plots' classification branch n is taken from the classes present in targets, but counts_pred is np.bincount(preds, minlength=n), which is longer than x whenever the model predicts a class index absent from the val targets; ax4.bar then raises on shape mismatch. Latent today.

nn/data_builder.py:143-144 — comment claims 'Multiple POs per variant — keep most recent'. data/po_line_items.csv has 645 rows and 645 distinct variant_ids, exactly one PO line each, so the sort_values/drop_duplicates is a no-op and no landed cost varies across POs.

nn/data_builder.py:351, :362, :371 — the addresses, support_tickets and support_message_features merges have no drop_duplicates while _load_refunds and _load_po_line_items do. Verified safe today (all five merge keys unique: orders 49,793, customers 22,440, addresses 22,440, variants 645, products 62, tickets 1,204), but one duplicate row in a refreshed CSV would silently multiply line items.

verdict: Working, well-built demo whose published results are mostly artifacts. The code is clean and the previous review's leakage fix did land correctly — but the same hand-maintained-map failure recurred a third time, and this run found three more key targets (resolved_by, product_type, city) that are one-column lookups, with REPORT.md confidently explaining two of them via the wrong mechanism. Health is in the write-up, not the engineering: the right move is to withdraw the numbers and add the structural test, not to build Phase 11. Blocked on a runnable Python env — no pip on the review box, so re-runs need Visesh's machine.
